tells.1: Em dash plus a tacked-on, sentimental closer ('help us get these young trees in the ground!')
tells.2: Slightly awkward smoothing ('meet your neighbours while we get the trees in the ground') that reads like a paraphrase
tells.4: Reworded flourishes ('60 saplings waiting to go in the ground', 'give these young trees a good start') that feel like stylistic rewriting rather than a notice
tells.6: Closing triplet ending in an exclamation ('come along, meet your neighbours and help us…!') is a mild padded-rhythm tell

reason: Version 5 has the unpolished feel of a real volunteer note ('21st', 'until', a run-on sentence), but it's clunky. Version 3 keeps the plain, natural voice while being the clearest and tightest, with nothing extra.
